newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds surge across the board.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds surge across the board.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed sharply higher on Monday led by a steep rise in CPI-linked bonds, traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): +0.09 pct to 103.21
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.06 pct at 102.59
Volume was moderate at 164 million shekels with most of the activity concentrated in the Makams.

"We saw very big demand surplus of 170 million shekels for CPI-linked bonds. Analysts have raised their inflation forecasts for 1997 from 8.5 percent to more than 10 percent and investors want to protect themselves by buying inflation-linked bonds," said Gidi Halperin of Meitav Securities and Investments.
"The sharp rise of dollar might lead to a steep rise in inflation," said Ron Weisberg of IBI Investment House.
"Yields on CPI-linked long bonds fell during the last few days from 4.3 percent to 4.2 percent and this trend is likely to continue with yields falling eventually to four percent," Weisberg said.
He added that unlinked bonds also rose but at a more moderate pace. Halperin said turnover in the unlinked Makams was high at 80 million shekels.

"Investors are buying short Makams because they offer the best protection for private investors who do not want to take any risks," Halperin said, noting that they offered good yields even with inflation ramping up.

Dollar-linked bonds also rose after the shekel weakened against the dollar. In the local forex market the representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.3530 shekels against 3.3480 shekels on Thursday.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
